interpretations: For each gender among customers reached through an invoice and its order, count distinct orders with at least one invoice; divide by the total distinct invoiced orders; return genders whose share exceeds the average share of those genders, with the difference between the two shares.

For each gender among customers reached through an invoice and its order, count invoice–order matches, counting an order once per invoice; divide by the total matches; return genders whose share exceeds the average share of those genders, with the difference between the two shares.
Count distinct invoiced orders by gender, including customers whose gender is NULL as one group; calculate each group’s share and return groups above the average share.
Count invoice–order matches by gender, including customers whose gender is NULL as one group; calculate each group’s share and return groups above the average share.
Count distinct invoiced orders by gender, but calculate the average share across every gender value in Customers, assigning zero share to gender values with no invoiced orders.
Count invoice–order matches by gender, but calculate the average share across every gender value in Customers, assigning zero share to gender values with no invoice–order matches.
For any of these counts and shares, report “how far above average” as the share minus the average share.
For any of these counts and shares, report “how far above average” as the excess divided by the average share.
Count distinct invoiced orders by non-NULL gender, include orders belonging to customers with NULL gender in the overall total, and average the shares across non-NULL genders with invoiced orders.
Count invoice–order matches by non-NULL gender, include matches belonging to customers with NULL gender in the overall total, and average the shares across non-NULL genders with matches.

Count distinct invoiced orders by non-NULL gender, include orders belonging to customers with NULL gender in the overall total, and average across all non-NULL gender values in Customers, assigning zero share where needed.

Count invoice–order matches by non-NULL gender, include matches belonging to customers with NULL gender in the overall total, and average across all non-NULL gender values in Customers, assigning zero share where needed.
queries:
WITH gender_orders AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count
    FROM Customers AS c
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
),
shares AS (
    SELECT
        gender,
        1.0 * order_count / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM gender_orders
)
SELECT
    gender,
    share - AVG(share) OVER () AS share_difference
FROM shares
WHERE share > (SELECT AVG(share) FROM shares)

WITH matches AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT i.invoice_number, o.order_id, c.gender
    FROM Invoices AS i
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
),
shares AS (
    SELECT gender,
           COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM matches) AS share
    FROM matches
    GROUP BY gender
)
SELECT gender,
       share - (SELECT AVG(share) FROM shares) AS share_difference
FROM shares
WHERE share > (SELECT AVG(share) FROM shares)

WITH gender_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender,
           COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS invoiced_order_count
    FROM Customers AS c
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
),
gender_shares AS (
    SELECT gender,
           invoiced_order_count,
           1.0 * invoiced_order_count
               / SUM(invoiced_order_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM gender_counts
)
SELECT gender, invoiced_order_count, share
FROM gender_shares
WHERE share > (SELECT AVG(share) FROM gender_shares)

WITH gender_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS match_count
    FROM Invoices AS i
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
),
gender_shares AS (
    SELECT gender,
           match_count,
           1.0 * match_count / SUM(match_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM gender_counts
)
SELECT gender, match_count, share
FROM gender_shares
WHERE share > (SELECT AVG(share) FROM gender_shares)

WITH gender_counts AS (
    SELECT
        c.gender,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE
            WHEN i.invoice_number IS NOT NULL THEN o.order_id
        END) AS invoiced_order_count
    FROM Customers AS c
    LEFT JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
),
gender_shares AS (
    SELECT
        gender,
        invoiced_order_count,
        COALESCE(
            1.0 * invoiced_order_count
                / NULLIF(SUM(invoiced_order_count) OVER (), 0),
            0
        ) AS share
    FROM gender_counts
)
SELECT
    gender,
    invoiced_order_count,
    AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share
FROM gender_shares

WITH gender_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(i.invoice_number) AS match_count
    FROM (SELECT DISTINCT gender FROM Customers) AS c
    LEFT JOIN Customers AS customer ON customer.gender IS c.gender
    LEFT JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = customer.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
)
SELECT AVG(
    CASE
        WHEN total_matches = 0 THEN 0.0
        ELSE 1.0 * match_count / total_matches
    END
) AS average_share
FROM (
    SELECT match_count, SUM(match_count) OVER () AS total_matches
    FROM gender_counts
)
